title: JWKS Pinned-Directory Check
description: Confirms a caller-supplied JWKS directory document matches a caller-pinned SHA-256 digest -- sha256(canonicalize(directory_jwks)) === pinned_digest -- before art-130 trusts the document's internal shape. Canonicalization is this codebase's one JCS/RFC-8785 canon (recursive key-sort, array order preserved), hashed as lowercase hex, so two honest callers hashing the same logical document land on the same digest. Zero network, zero key hosting: both the directory document and the pinned digest are supplied by the caller, never fetched, cached, or served by this tool. Chains before art-130 in the visa-tap-agent-verification chain, so a substituted directory fails before its shape is even checked.

directory_jwks.description: The JWKS directory document the caller fetched, to be checked against the pin.

pinned_digest.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex digest (64 chars) the caller computed and stored out-of-band at directory-onboarding time, over the canonical JWKS bytes.

pinned_digest_well_formed.description: True only if pinned_digest is present and matches 64 lowercase-or-mixed-case hex characters.

mcp_tool_definition.name: check_jwks_pinned_directory
mcp_tool_definition.description: Confirms a caller-supplied JWKS directory document matches a caller-pinned SHA-256 digest, before art-130 trusts its shape. Zero network, zero key hosting -- both inputs are caller-supplied.

source: authored by BUILD-BOTAUTH-JWKSPIN-1 per research/SPEC-BOTAUTH-NONCE-VISA-1-2026-08-09.md SS3/SS5/SS6(b); canonicalization decision (SS6(b), flagged unresolved by the spec) is documented in the kernel file's own header comment -- reuses _hash.mjs's JCS/cgCanon path via a guest-safe inlined transcription, the same shape proven by art-476.
